Write each story\\'s tests first and confirm they FAIL before implementing.\\n\\n**Organization**: Tasks are grouped by user story to enable independent implementation and testing of each story.\\n\\n## Format: `[ID] [P?] [Story] Description`\\n\\n- **[P]**: Can run in parallel (different files, no dependencies)\\n- **[Story]**: Which user story this task belongs to (e.g., US1, US2, US3)\\n- Include exact file paths in descriptions\\n\\n**Source of truth**: implementation in `src/cachetools/tagged.py` (new file); own tests in `tests/test_tagged.py` (new file). Public gate: `acceptance_public.py` (unmodified). Upstream tests and existing `src/cachetools/__init__.py` must remain unchanged.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Phase 1: Setup (Shared Infrastructure)\\n\\n**Purpose**: Create the new module and test file skeletons (no behavior yet)\\n\\n- [ ] T001 [P] Create `src/cachetools/tagged.py` skeleton: module docstring, `from copy import deepcopy`, `from . import LRUCache` (or `from cachetools import LRUCache` — pick one, no circular import), and an empty `class TaggedCache:` placeholder\\n- [ ] T002 [P] Create `tests/test_tagged.py` skeleton: `from cachetools.tagged import TaggedCache` import plus one trivial smoke test (construct `TaggedCache(4)`) so the test file is runnable\\n\\n**Checkpoint**: `PYTHONPATH=src:. python -m pytest tests/test_tagged.py -q` collects and passes the smoke test; `git status --porcelain` shows no modified tracked files\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Phase 2: Foundational (Blocking Prerequisites)\\n\\n**Purpose**: Core helpers that every user story depends on (all in `src/cachetools/tagged.py`)\\n\\n**⚠️ CRITICAL**: No user story work can begin until this phase is complete\\n\\n- [ ] T003 Implement `_validate_maxsize(value)` in `src/cachetools/tagged.py` raising `ValueError` unless `isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) and value > 0` (R03; covers `True`, `False`, `0`, negatives, floats, strings)\\n- [ ] T004 Implement `_normalize_tags(tags)` in `src/cachetools/tagged.py` per research.md R3/R10: reject bare `str` with `ValueError`; require an iterable (else `ValueError`); consume it exactly once via a single `list(iter(tags))` pass (generators safe, R06); reject any non-`str` element with `ValueError`; return `frozenset(...)` (dedup, R01). No state may be touched before it returns\\n- [ ] T005 Implement `__init__(self, maxsize)` in `src/cachetools/tagged.py`: validate via T003, then create `self._cache = LRUCache(maxsize)`, `self._entry_tags = {}` (key -> frozenset of tags), `self._tag_keys = {}` (tag -> set of keys)\\n- [ ] T006 Implement `_remove(self, key)` in `src/cachetools/tagged.py` — the single choke point (data-model.md invariant 3): delete `self._cache[key]` (LRU order cleans itself), pop `self._entry_tags[key]`, remove key from every tag\\'s set in `self._tag_keys`, drop tag entries that become empty. Every removal path (put-eviction, invalidate, invalidate_many, resize) MUST go through this method\\n\\n**Checkpoint**: helpers unit-testable in isolation (bad maxsize raises; `_normalize_tags` rejects `\\\\'ab\\\\'`, `1`, `(1,)`, consumes a generator once); no user story code yet\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Phase 3: User Story 1 - Store and retrieve tagged entries (Priority: P1) 🎯 MVP\\n\\n**Goal**: `put`/`get` with deep-copy detachment both directions, tag registration, `KeyError` on miss, `len`/`in` (R01, R06)\\n\\n**Independent Test**: `PYTHONPATH=src:. python -m pytest tests/test_tagged.py -q -k \\\\'us1 or put or get or detach\\\\'` — put then get returns an equal but distinct object; mutating a returned nested list does not affect a later get; missing key raises `KeyError`; `len`/`in` correct\\n\\n### Tests for User Story 1 (write first, must FAIL) ⚠️\\n\\n- [ ] T007 [P] [US1] Add tests in `tests/test_tagged.py`: put/get round-trip equality; input copied (mutate original value after put, get returns original); output detached (mutate returned nested list/dict, re-get shows stored value intact, R06); `get` missing key raises `KeyError`; tags deduplicated (`put(k, v, [\\\\'a\\\\', \\\\'a\\\\', \\\\'b\\\\'])` behaves like `[\\\\'a\\\\', \\\\'b\\\\']`); `len(cache)` counts live entries; `key in cache` works\\n\\n### Implementation for User Story 1\\n\\n- [ ] T008 [US1] Implement `put(self, key, value, tags=())` in `src/cachetools/tagged.py`: normalize tags via T004 FIRST (invalid tags -> `ValueError`, cache unchanged — R01/R03); on existing key remove old tag memberships via T006 before replacing; store `deepcopy(value)` into `self._cache[key]` (one capacity slot per value, R03); register new tag memberships; LRU eviction of overflow happens through T006 (R02)\\n- [ ] T009 [US1] Implement `get(self, key)` in `src/cachetools/tagged.py`: `self._cache[key]` (raises `KeyError` on miss and refreshes recency on hit — R02), return `deepcopy(value)` (R06)\\n- [ ] T010 [US1] Implement `__len__`, `__contains__`, `__iter__` in `src/cachetools/tagged.py` delegating to `self._cache` (len counts live entries, R02)\\n\\n**Checkpoint**: US1 independently testable — `acceptance_public.py`-style put/get flows pass; story tests green\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Phase 4: User Story 2 - Invalidate by tag and evict with clean state (Priority: P2)\\n\\n**Goal**: `invalidate(tag)` exact removal with count; no stale tag memberships after eviction/replacement; recency refresh on get and on overwrite-put (Claim-A) (R02)\\n\\n**Independent Test**: `PYTHONPATH=src:. python -m pytest tests/test_tagged.py -q -k \\\\'invalidate or evict or recency\\\\'` — invalidate removes exactly the tagged entries and returns the count; after LRU eviction the evicted key\\\\'s tags no longer match; overwriting a key via put makes it most-recently-used (Claim-A)\\n\\n### Tests for User Story 2 (write first, must FAIL) ⚠️\\n\\n- [ ] T011 [P] [US2] Add tests in `tests/test_tagged.py`: `invalidate(tag)` removes exactly entries carrying the tag and returns the count (0 for unknown tag); replacing a key with new tags removes its old memberships; LRU-evicted key leaves no stale membership (re-put an evicted key with unrelated tags, then `invalidate(old_tag)` must not touch it); `get` refreshes recency (eviction order changes after get); overwrite-put refreshes recency making the key most-recently-used (Claim-A extension — evict until it is the last survivor); `len` tracks invalidation\\n\\n### Implementation for User Story 2\\n\\n- [ ] T012 [US2] Implement `invalidate(self, tag)` in `src/cachetools/tagged.py`: `keys = set(self._tag_keys.get(tag, ()))`; remove each via T006; return `len(keys)`; drop the tag\\\\'s index entry when empty. Verify the put-eviction path (T008) already routes through T006; if not, fix it (R02 stale-membership guarantee)\\n\\n**Checkpoint**: US1 + US2 independently testable; no stale memberships observable in any test\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Phase 5: User Story 3 - Safe construction and replacement (Priority: P3)\\n\\n**Goal**: `maxsize` validation (positive int, bool excluded) and atomic replacement — invalid input leaves old value/tags/recency unchanged (R03)\\n\\n**Independent Test**: `PYTHONPATH=src:. python -m pytest tests/test_tagged.py -q -k \\\\'maxsize or atomic or replace\\\\'` — `TaggedCache(True/False/0/-1/1.5/\\\\'5\\\\')` all raise `ValueError`; `put(k, v, bad_tags)` on an existing key leaves old value, old tags, and recency position unchanged\\n\\n### Tests for User Story 3 (write first, must FAIL) ⚠️\\n\\n- [ ] T013 [P] [US3] Add tests in `tests/test_tagged.py`: constructor rejects `True`, `False`, `0`, `-1`, `1.5`, `\\\\'5\\\\'` with `ValueError`; invalid replacement (bare-string tags, non-string tag element) on an existing key leaves old value (deep-copy-equal), old tag memberships, and recency order unchanged (verify recency via a subsequent eviction); every value costs exactly one slot regardless of size (fill `TaggedCache(2)` with large nested values, third put evicts exactly one)\\n\\n### Implementation for User Story 3\\n\\n- [ ] T014 [US3] Audit/harden `put` in `src/cachetools/tagged.py`: tag validation (T004) and value handling must complete BEFORE any mutation of `self._cache`/indexes on the replacement path (invalid input -> zero state change, R03); confirm `__init__` uses T003 (R03). Fix any ordering gap found\\n\\n**Checkpoint**: all R01-R03 behavior green; `acceptance_public.py` passes if it covers milestone-1 scope\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Phase 6: User Story 4 - Bulk invalidation with any/all semantics (Priority: P2)\\n\\n**Goal**: `invalidate_many(tags, mode=\\\\'any\\\\')` — union/intersection matching, distinct-key count, empty-removes-zero in both modes, pre-mutation validation, `invalidate` parity (R04)\\n\\n**Independent Test**: `PYTHONPATH=src:. python -m pytest tests/test_tagged.py -q -k \\\\'invalidate_many\\\\'` plus quickstart.md scenario 5 — `{a},{b},{a,b}` entries: any->3, all->1; empty list/tuple/exhausted generator -> 0 in both modes; invalid mode/tags raise `ValueError` with state unchanged; single-tag call equals `invalidate(tag)`\\n\\n### Tests for User Story 4 (write first, must FAIL) ⚠️\\n\\n- [ ] T015 [P] [US4] Add tests in `tests/test_tagged.py`: any-mode union removal and distinct-key count; all-mode intersection removal; duplicate requested tags deduplicated (count not inflated); empty requested tags (`[]`, `()`, exhausted generator) remove zero in BOTH modes (superseded design note disproven — SC-006); invalid mode (`\\\\'nope\\\\'`, `None`) raises `ValueError` with cache unchanged; invalid tags (bare string, non-string element, non-iterable) raise `ValueError` with cache unchanged; generator tag source consumed once; `invalidate_many([t])` result identical to `invalidate(t)`\\n\\n### Implementation for User Story 4\\n\\n- [ ] T016 [US4] Implement `invalidate_many(self, tags, mode=\\\\'any\\\\')` in `src/cachetools/tagged.py` per research.md R8: validate `mode in (\\\\'any\\\\', \\\\'all\\\\')` FIRST, then `requested = _normalize_tags(tags)`; if `not requested: return 0`; matched = union of `self._tag_keys[t]` (any) or `set.intersection(*[self._tag_keys[t] for t in requested])` (all); remove each matched key via T006; return the distinct count\\n\\n**Checkpoint**: US4 independently testable;
